Xxxx vs State Of Kerala on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68109839/
1  Dated this the 4th day of October, 2024  JUDGMENT
The accused in S.C.No.506 of 2018 on the files of the Special Court for the trial of offences under the PoCSO Act, Kottayam is the appellant.

As per the judgment dated 21.12.2021 the appellant was convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(f), (i) and (n) of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (IPC) and under Section 4 r/w 3(b) & (d) and Section 6 r/w 5(l), (m) & (n) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (PoCSO) Act, 2012.

sentences.text:
He is sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.50,000/- each under Section 376(2)(i),
(f) & (n) of the IPC with a default sentence of rigorous imprisonment for another one year.
The terms of the substantive sentence are ordered to be run concurrently.
Assailing the said judgment of conviction and sentence, this appeal has been filed under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Code).

The case of the prosecution is the following:
PW1, the victim, was aged 9 years during the relevant time.
She went to the house of the appellant for a two days' stay owing to the school vacation.
The appellant is the husband of the sister of PW1's mother.
On 16.05.2017 at about 1.30 p.m. the appellant took PW1 to the bathroom behind his house, which is at Manjoor, and subjected her to penetrative sexual assault.
He committed similar acts at about 1.30 p.m. on 17.05.2017 also.
3. PW1 told about the incident to her friends while in the school.

One of her friends, Shivani,
informed the matter to their teacher.
The incident was accordingly informed in the Child Line.
As informed from the Child Line, PW9, recorded Ext.P1 FI statement from PW1, based on which the crime was registered by PW10.
Ext. P7
is the FIR.
After investigation, a final report was laid before the court.
4. At the trial, PWs.1 to 14 were examined and Exts.P1 to P15 were marked on the side of the prosecution.
After closing the prosecution evidence, the appellant was 2024:KER:73889 questioned under Section 313(1)(b) of the Code.
He stated that the case was foisted against him.
He added that PW2, the mother of the victim, had been in inimical terms with him and due to that enmity, the case was fabricated.
On the side of the appellant, DWs.1 and 2 were examined and Exts.D1 to D5 were marked.
Ext.X1 was also marked.
After hearing both sides, the trial court held that the evidence of PW1 is devoid of any blemishes.
Trusting her evidence, the trial court found the appellant guilty of the offences.
The appellant assails the finding leading to his conviction on many grounds.

Unreliable nature of PW1 which contain several inconsistencies, the delay, absence of any independent evidence or medical evidence, non-examination of friends of PW1, hostility between PW2 and the appellant, etc. are the grounds urged to assail the impugned judgment.

2 5.
Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Public Prosecutor.
6. PW1 was aged 9 years at the time of occurrence.
Her date of birth is 27.04.2008.
Ext . P8
is the birth certificate.
It was duly proved by the Registrar of Births, PW12.
PW14, the Headmaster of the school where PW1 first studied proved Ext.P15, which is the extract of the relevant pages of the admission register.
Nothing has come on record to show that they have stated in court any incorrect facts.
Exts. P8
and P15
are duly proved.
PW1 and her mother PW2 deposed in court that date of birth of PW1 is 27.04.2008, which is the date reflects from the said documents also.
The said evidence duly proved that PW1 was born on 27.04.2008 and her age on the dates of occurrence was nine years.
7. PW1 narrated about the incident in court.

Her narration about the incident in the words of the trial court is as follows:
"12. PW1 deposed that her mother's sister Bindhuchitta along with her husband Kochayi and their two children were residing at Manjoor and she was sexually assaulted while staying there.

She used to visit Bindhuchitta's house and stay there at times and that her grandparents took her to the said house in the month of May,
2017.

And that on 16/05/2017 in the afternoon Gadha chechi was lying ill and when Kochayi (the accused) came to have lunch, he took her to bath 2024:KER:73889 room outside the house, removed her baniyan and pant and stirred her private parts and also licked there

. She also deposed that Kochayi asked her to hold his penis but,
she did not hold it and when Gadha Chechi called her she was pushed out of the bathroom.
It is further deposed that on the next day this was repeated and when Gadha Chechi made enquiry from the kitchen side, Kochayi allowed her to go out of the bathroom.

She also deposed that Gokul, son of the accused, on the same day took her to her grandmother's house and as she felt pain while urinating, she revealed the incident to her grandmother and her grandmother told her not to tell it to others and if she disclosed it to others, Kochayi would be taken by police.

It is also deposed that when she was in the school hostel at Ettumanoor while she was in 5th standard, she told about the incident to her friend Shivani and she in turn told the teacher and the teacher informed the same to the Childline.
PW1 identified her signature in Ext.P1 and deposed that police came to hostel and recorded her statement.
She identified the accused in the dock also.
She further deposed that the true facts were stated before the Magistrate and she identified her name and thump impression in Ext.P2."
8. There is no witness to the occurrence.

Having the incident allegedly taken place inside the bathroom and nobody other than the ailing daughter of the appellant been there in 2024:KER:73889 the house, there could not be any occurrence witness.
Of course, PW1 deposed that on the second day ie., 17.05.2017 daughter of the appellant came near the bathroom and called out what was they doing.
Ext.P2 is the statement given by PW1 to the Magistrate under Section 164 of the Code.
In it she stated that the daughter of the appellant saw the incident on the second day.

Xxxx vs State Of Kerala on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68109839/
3
Anyhow, she was not cited as a witness by the prosecution.

Therefore, only direct evidence that can be relied on by the prosecution is that of PW1.
9.

The prosecution further would rely on the circumstances such as PW1 was allowed to stay for two days in the house of the appellant, the incident came to light through the school authorities,
indifferent behaviour of PW1 after the incident and the statement she had given to PW5, the Doctor,
to establish the guilt of the appellant.
The learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the evidence of PW1 is totally inconsistent in terms of the dates of occurrence and the way in which the incident came to be disclosed.
Along with that the delay and the hostility existed between PW2 and 2024:KER:73889 the wife of the appellant, who are sisters, the evidence of PW1 cannot be trusted.
It is submitted that in order to draw a presumption under Section 29 of the PoCSO Act, the basic facts must be proved.
But in this case, the uncorroborated testimony of PW1 is not at all creditworthy so as to prove even the basic facts.
10. Going by the evidence of PW1, after her stay for two days, she was taken back to her house by the appellant's son.
But how she went to the house is not clear.
She stated in court that her grandparents took her to the house of the appellant.
She deposed before the Magistrate that her elder brother took her to that house.
PW3 is the grandmother.
She denied having taken PW1 to the house of the appellant.
PW4 is the brother of PW1.
He stated that he himself and the victim used to go to the house of the appellant and stay there during holidays.
He claimed that it was he who took PW1 to the house of the appellant on the day prior to the date of incident.
He did not remember whether his grandmother was with him.

The said inconsistency may not have much 2024:KER:73889 relevance,
when the evidence shows that PW1 used to go and stay in the house of the appellant.
However, in the light of the inconsistency concerning the dates of occurrence, the said aspects assumes relevance.
11. Leaving apart the evidence of PWs.3 and 4, only evidence to prove the dates of occurrence is that of PW1.
Her mother, PW2 is not definite as to when the incident occurred and therefore her evidence is not available to prove that fact.
Of course, she stated that the incident occurred on 16.05.2017 and 17.05.2017, but the same was on the basis of the information she obtained from PW1 more than after a month.
In her presence only PW1 gave the dates in Ext.P1 as 16.09.2016 and 17.09.2016.
In the nature of the said evidence, a meticulous analysis of the evidence of PW1 concerning the dates of occurrence is necessary.
12. Ext.P1 F.I.statement was recorded by PW9 on 31.07.2017.
On getting information from the Child Line authorities, PW9 recorded the statement.
It has come out that PW1 was admitted at the Model Residential School, 2024:KER:73889 Ettumanoor at the beginning of the academic year.
Following complaints of her indifferent behaviour, PW2 took her to St.Thomas High School, Kallara, where she was admitted.
While in that school, PW1 disclosed about the incident to one of her friends, who in turn informed the teacher.
After that, the Child Line authorities counselled the child and Ext.P1 statement was happened to be recorded from her.
13. The specific assertion in Ext.P1 is that on the Onam days she went to the house of the appellant and the incident occurred on 16.09.2016 and 17.09.2016.

When the said dates were deposed Xxxx vs State Of Kerala on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68109839/
4 connecting to Onam, it is not able to assume that PW1 could not correctly remember the date.
While filing the final report, the dates of incidents were corrected as 16.05.2017 and 17.05.2017.

If those were the actual dates of occurrence, there was absolutely no probability for PW1 connecting the dates with Onam, especially when she gave Ext.P1 statement on 31.07.2017, which was not a far distant date.
In the said circumstances, it is not possible to safely rely on the version of PW1 to find when the incident occurred.
may further be noted that if PW1 went to the house of the appellant only once, her evidence could be given credence dehors such an inconsistency.
But the evidence shows that she used to go to the house of the appellant during every Onam, Christmas and summer vacations.
That adds to the doubt about the version regarding the dates of the incident.
14. PW1 gave Ext.P2 statement to the Magistrate on 18.08.2017.
In that statement, PW1 did not state anything about the date.
She maintained that she did not remember the date.
She asserted before the Magistrate that she was taken to the house of the appellant by her brother, PW4 as against her version in court that the grandparents took her to that house.
Those contradictions were brought out while she was examined before the court.
No explanation for the discrepancy has come out.
Of course, at the time of examination before the court, PW1 was aged only 13 years.
While deposing about an incident that occurred at the age of 9 years, inability for her to recollect every aspect of the matter cannot be ignored.
But when only evidence that could be used 2024:KER:73889 to prove the charge is that of PW1, the victim, such inconsistencies cannot fully be overlooked.
15. Considering the nature of the alleged incident, the possibility of having any serious injury suggestive of such a sexual assault is remote.
PW5 did not notice any injuries and found hymen of PW1 intact.
Thus, there is no medical evidence to support the case of the prosecution.
I am saying so not in ignorance of the unlikely chance of there having any medical indication, especially when the medical examination was after about 1 months.
But the fact remains is that there is no medical evidence.
The history of sexual assault by the appellant was stated to PW5.

In the absence of any clinical indication suggestive of such a sexual assault, the statement of PW1 to PW5 regarding the sexual assault, which was given after such a distance of time, can be treated only as a hearsay information.
Therefore, the evidence of PW5 is not available to corroborate the version of PW1 in court.
16. The evidence thus, the prosecution can rely on is the oral testimony of PW1.
When PW2 and PW4 did not state 2024:KER:73889 anything before the court, which may amount to a res gestae or give any corroborative statement, oral testimony of PW1 stands proved.
17. PWs.1 and 2 admitted that PW2 and her sister who is the wife of the appellant were not in good terms; not even in talking terms.
When the evidence of PW1 is considered in that context, the same cannot be acted upon to prove the basic facts enabling to draw the presumption under Section 29 of the PoCSO Act.
The proposition of law is trite that the evidence of the victim is sufficient to enter a conviction in a charge of rape.

But the court should be able to trust the evidence of the victim,
atleast, on the basic facts.
Dates of the alleged occurrence were stated totally discrepantly.
How PW1 reached the house of the appellant is not cogent.
The friends of PW1 to whom she disclosed about the incident first are not examined.

Reason why the daughter of the appellant, who could state about the presence of PW1 and the appellant together at the time of the alleged incident is not cited or Xxxx vs State Of Kerala on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68109839/
5 examined by the prosecution.
Those aspects created doubt 2024:KER:73889 about the version of PW1 regarding the incident.

Hence, I hold that the trial court went wrong in holding that the evidence tendered by the prosecution proved necessary the basic facts enabling the court to draw a presumption under Section 29 of the PoCSO Act.
The inevitable consequence is that the appellant is entitled to get the benefit of doubt.
Hence, this appeal is allowed and the appellant is acquitted.
The appellant shall be released from the jail forthwith and set at liberty.

Sd/-
P.G. AJITHKUMAR, JUDGE dkr Xxxx vs State Of Kerala on 4 October, 2024
